-detach.description: -detach: Indicates that no more data will be added to the chart and that the identifying number is available for a new USER_GRAPH definition. The chart window remains visible and all mouse functions for the chart remain functional.

-active.description: -active: Allows plotting of data to the chart to be suspended or resumed. Default is true if -active is not included. ( True or False ): If false , plotting of data is suspended; if true , plotting is resumed. If neither true nor false is entered on the line, true is assumed. Optionally, t [ rue ] or f [ alse ].

-plot_csv_file.description: Writes the USER_GRAPH data to a comma-separated-values file (newer PHREEQC versions; analogous to -plot_tsv_file).

USER_PRINT.description: This keyword data block is used to define a Basic program that prints user-defined quantities to the output file. Any Basic “PRINT” statement will write to the output file.

-start.description: -start: Indicates the start of the Basic program. Optional. numbered Basic statement: A valid Basic language statement that must be numbered. The statements are evaluated in the order of the line numbers. Statements and functions that are available through the Basic interpreter are listed in The Basic Interpreter, tables 7 and 8.

-end.description: -end: Indicates the end of the Basic program. Optional. Note the hyphen is required to avoid a conflict with the keyword END .

USER_PUNCH.description: This keyword data block is used to define Basic programs that print user-defined quantities to a selected-output file. Multiple SELECTED_OUTPUT definitions using different values of n are possible; each is used to write a different file. USER_PUNCH n writes to the file defined in SELECTED_OUTPUT n. Any Basic “PUNCH” statement will write to the selected-output file.

-headings.description: -headings: Headings will appear on the first line of the selected-output file. Optionally, heading , headings , or -h [ eadings ]. list of column headings: White-space-delimited (any combination of spaces and tabs) list of column headings.

-start.description: -start: Indicates the start of the Basic program. Optional. numbered Basic statement: A valid Basic language statement that must be numbered. The statements are evaluated in the order of the line numbers. Statements and functions that are available through the Basic interpreter are listed in The Basic Interpreter, tables 7 and 8.

-end.description: -end: Indicates the end of the Basic program. Optional. Note the hyphen is required to avoid a conflict with the keyword END .

ACT.description: Activity of an aqueous, exchange, or surface species.

ALK.description: Alkalinity of solution, equivalents per kilogram water.

APHI.description: The A(phi) parameter of the Pitzer formulation of aqueous thermodynamics at the current solution conditions.

CALC_VALUE.description: Value calculated by Basic function (here, R(D)_OH-) defined in CALCULATE_VALUES data block.

CEIL.description: Smallest integer not less than a.

CELL_NO.description: Cell number in TRANSPORT or ADVECTION calculations; otherwise solution or mix number.

CHANGE_POR.description: Modifies the porosity in a cell, used only in multicomponent diffusion calculations (keyword TRANSPORT ). Here, porosity of cell cell_no is set to 0.21.

CHANGE_SURF.description: Changes the diffusion coefficient of (part of) a surface ( SURFACE ), and renames the surface (if names are different). This function is for modeling transport, deposition, and remobilization of colloids. It is used in conjunction with multicomponent diffusion in a TRANSPORT data block. Here: take a fraction 0.2 of Hfo and rename it Sorbedhfo with a diffusion coefficient of 0, in cell cell_no.

CHARGE_BALANCE.description: Charge balance of a solution, equivalents.

COLOR.description: USER_GRAPH plot command: sets the color of the current curve.

CURRENT_A.description: The electrical current through the column, in amperes, when simulating electro-migration in TRANSPORT.

DEBYE_LENGTH.description: The Debye length, typically notated kappa^-1, is related to the decay of the surface potential with distance from the surface. Theory says that the potential at distance d from the surface is equal to psi0*exp(d/DL), where psi0 is the surface potential and DL is the Debye length. The length is inversely related to ionic strength.

DELTA_H_PHASE.description: Delta H in KJ/mol. If an analytic expression exists, Delta H is at reaction temperature; otherwise Delta H at 25 C.

DELTA_H_SPECIES.description: Delta H in KJ/mol. If an analytic expression exists, Delta H is at reaction temperature, otherwise Delta H at 25 C.

DESCRIPTION.description: Description associated with current solution or current mixture.

DH_A.description: Debye-Hückel A parameter in the activity coefficient equation, (mol/kg) -0.5 .

DH_AV.description: Debye-Hückel limiting slope of specific volume vs. ionic strength, (cm 3 /mol) (mol/kg) -0.5 .

DH_B.description: Debye-Hückel B parameter in the activity coefficient equation, angstrom -1 (mol/kg) -0.5 .

DIFF_C.description: Diffusion coefficient at 25 C for the specified aqueous species.

DIST.description: Distance to midpoint of cell in TRANSPORT calculations, cell number in ADVECTION calculations, -99 in all other calculations.

EDL.description: Moles of element in the diffuse layer of a surface. The number of moles does not include the specifically sorbed species. The surface name should be used, not a surface site name (that is, no underscore).

EDL_SPECIES.signature: EDL_SPECIES(surf$, count, name$, moles, area, thickness)
EDL_SPECIES.description: Returns the total number of moles of species in the diffuse layer. The The arguments to the function are as follows: surf$ is the name of a surface, such as "Hfo", excluding the site type (such as "_s"); count is the number of species in the diffuse layer; name$ is an array of size count that contains the names of aqueous species in the diffuse layer of surface surf$; moles is an array of size count that contains the number of moles of each aqueo…

ELSE.signature: IF expr THEN statement ELSE statement
ELSE.description: Alternative branch of an IF ... THEN statement.

EOL$.description: End of line string that is appropriate for the operating system.

EOL_NOTAB$.description: Omits the tab that is normally printed after EOL$.

EQUI.description: Moles of a phase in the equilibrium-phase assemblage.

ERASE.description: Revert the Basic variable to an undimensioned variable so that it can be used as a scalar or dimensioned with another DIM statement. Applies only to variables that have been dimensioned with a DIM statement.

EXISTS.description: Determines if a value has been stored with a PUT statement for the list of one or more subscripts.The function equals 1 if a value has been stored and 0 if no value has been stored. Values are stored in global storage with PUT and are accessible by any Basic program. See description of PUT for more details.

FLOOR.description: Largest integer not greater than a.

FOR.signature: FOR i = n TO m STEP k NEXT i

F_VISC.description: Returns the fractional contribution of a species to viscosity of the solution when parameters are defined for the species with -viscosity. Actually, it gives the contribution of the species to the B and D terms in the Jones-Dole equation, assuming that the A term is small. The fractional contribution can be negative, for example F_VISC ("K+") is usually less than zero.

GAS.description: Moles of a gas component in the gas phase.

GAS_P.description: Pressure of the GAS_PHASE (atm), either specified for a fixed-pressure gas phase, or calculated for a fixed-volume gas phase. Related functions are PR_P and PRESSURE.

GAS_VM.description: Molar volume (L/mol, liter per mole) of the GAS_PHASE (calculated with Peng-Robinson).

GET.description: Retrieves the value that is identified by the list of one or more subscripts. The value is zero if PUT has not been used to store a value for the set of subscripts. Values stored in global storage with PUT are accessible by any Basic program. See description of PUT for more details.

GET_POR.description: Porosity in a cell (here, cell 10), used in conjunction with Basic function CHANGE_POR in multicomponent diffusion.

GFW.description: Returns the gram formula weight of the specified formula.

GOSUB.description: Go to subroutine at line number.

GRAPH_SY.description: Used in USER_GRAPH data block to define the Y values for points plotted on the secondary Y axis. Here, pH is the Y value for points plotted on the secondary Y axis. See the description of the USER_GRAPH keyword for more details.

GRAPH_X.description: Used in USER_GRAPH data block to define the X values for points. Here, Ca in mg/L is the X value for points of the chart. See the description of the USER_GRAPH keyword for more details.

GRAPH_Y.description: Used in USER_GRAPH data block to define the Y values for points plotted on the primary Y axis. Here, F in mg/L is the Y value for points. See the description of the USER_GRAPH keyword for more details.

IF.signature: IF ( expr ) THEN statement ELSE statement
IF.description: If, then, else statement (on one line; a \ may be used to concatenate lines).

INSTR.description: The character position of the beginning of string b$ in a$ ; 0 if not found.

KAPPA.description: Compressibility of pure water at current pressure and temperature.

KINETICS_FORMULA$.description: KINETICS_FORMULA$ returns a string that contains the first argument of the argument list if the kinetic reaction defined by the first argument is found, or a blank string if not. In addition, values are returned for count, elt$, and coef. Count is the dimension of the elt$ and coef arrays. Elt$ is a character array with the name of each element in the chemical formula defined for the kinetic reaction.

KIN_DELTA.description: Moles of a kinetic reactant that reacted during the current calculation.

KIN_TIME.description: Time interval in seconds of the last kinetic integration. KIN_DELTA("CH2O")/KIN_TIME will give the average rate over the time interval for reaction CH2O.

LA.description: Log10 of activity of an aqueous, exchange, or surface species.

LG.description: Log10 of the activity coefficient for an aqueous species.

LINE_WIDTH.description: USER_GRAPH plot command: sets the line width of the current curve.

LIST_S_S.description: Returns the sum of the moles of components in a solid solution and the composition of the solid solution. The first argument is an input value specifying the name of the solid solution. Count is an output variable containing the number of components in the solid solution. Comp$ is an output character array containing the names of each component in the solid solution.

LK_NAMED.description: The value calculated by a named expression defined in the MIX_EQUILIBRIUM_PHASES data block.

LK_PHASE.description: Log10 of the equilibrium constant for a phase defined in the PHASES data block.

LK_SPECIES.description: Log10 of the equilibrium constant for an aqueous, exchange, or surface species.

LM.description: Log10 of molality of an aqueous, exchange, or surface species.

LTRIM.description: Trims white space from the beginning of string a$ .

M.description: Current moles of the kinetic reactant for which the rate is being calculated (see KINETICS ).

M0.description: Initial moles of the kinetic reactant for which the rate is being calculated (see KINETICS ).

MCD_JCONC.description: MCD_JCONC returns the flux for an aqueous species calculated by the first term of equation 10. The function ignores interlayer diffusion and only applies to multicomponent diffusion.

MCD_JTOT.description: MCD_JTOT returns the flux for an aqueous species as calculated by equation 10 in the description of the TRANSPORT keyword in the PHREEQC 3 manual. The function ignores interlayer diffusion and only applies to multicomponent diffusion.

MEANG.description: Calculates the mean activity coefficient for a salt listed in a MEAN_GAMMAS data block.

MID$.signature: MID$( string, n ) MID$( string, n, m )
MID$.description: Extract characters from position n to end of string. Extract m characters from string starting at position n .

MISC1.description: Mole fraction of component 2 at the beginning of the miscibility gap, returns 1.0 if there is no miscibility gap (see SOLID_SOLUTIONS ).

MISC2.description: Mole fraction of component 2 at the end of the miscibility gap, returns 1.0 if there is no miscibility gap (see SOLID_SOLUTIONS ).

MOL.description: Molality of an aqueous, exchange, or surface species.

NEXT.signature: FOR i = n1 TO n2 ... NEXT i

NO_NEWLINES.description: Suppresses newlines in PUNCH output so all values print on one line.

ON.signature: ON expr GOTO line1 , line2 , ... ON expr GOSUB line1 , line2 , ...
ON.description: If the value of the expression, rounded to an integer, is N , go to the N th line number in the list. If N is less than one or greater than the number of line numbers listed, execution continues at the next statement after the ON statement.

OSMOTIC.description: Osmotic coefficient if using the Pitzer or SIT aqueous model, otherwise 0.0, unitless.

PAD.description: Pads a$ with spaces to a total of i characters; returns a copy of a$ if the length of a$ is more than i characters.

PARM.description: The ith item in the parameter array defined in KINETICS data block.

PHASE_FORMULA$.description: Chemical formula of a phase, as a character string.

PHASE_VM.description: Returns the molar volume for a mineral (cm 3 /mol). The molar volume is defined for the mineral in PHASES with the -vm option. Use the Basic function GAS_VM for gas components.

PLOT_XY.signature: PLOT_XY tot("Ca") * 40.08e3, tot("F") * 19e3, color = Blue, symbol = Circle, symbol_size = 6, y-axis = 1, line_width = 0
PLOT_XY.description: Used in USER_GRAPH data block to define the points to chart; here, Ca in mg/L is the X value for points, F in mg/L is the Y value for points, the symbols are blue circles, the points are plotted relative to the Y axis, and no line connects the points. See the description of the USER_GRAPH keyword for more details.

POT_V.description: Potential in a cell, in Volts.

PRESSURE.description: Current pressure applied to the solution (atm). PRESSURE is a specified value except for fixed-volume GAS_PHASE calculations.

PR_P.description: Pressure (atm) of a gas component in a Peng-Robinson GAS_PHASE.

PR_PHI.description: Fugacity coefficient of a gas component in a Peng-Robinson GAS_PHASE.

PUT.description: Saves value of x in global storage that is identified by a sequence of one or more subscripts. Value of x can be retrieved with GET( i1[, i2, ... ]) and a set of subscripts can be tested to determine if a value has been stored with EXISTS( i1 [ , i2, ... ]). PUT may be used in CALCULATE_VALUES , RATES , USER_GRAPH , USER_PRINT , or USER_PUNCH Basic programs to store a value. The value may be retrieved by any of these Basic programs.

QBRN.description: The Born parameter for calculating the temperature dependence of the specific volume of an aqueous species at infinite dilution. This is the pressure derivative of the relative dielectric constant of water multiplied by 41.84 bar cm 3 /cal (bar cubic centimeter per calorie): , cm 3 /mol

REM.description: At beginning of line, line is a remark with no effect on the calculations.

RESTORE.description: Set pointer to DATA statement at line for subsequent READ.

RHO.description: Density of solution, kilograms per liter.

RHO_0.description: Density of pure water at the current temperature and pressure, kilograms per liter.

RTRIM.description: Trims white space from the end of string a$ .

RXN.description: Moles of reaction as defined in -steps in REACTION data block for a batch-reaction calculation; otherwise zero.

SAVE.description: Moles of kinetic reactant for a time step in a rates function or the value returned from a CALCULATE_VALUES function.

SETDIFF_C.description: Sets -dw for a species (see SOLUTION_SPECIES), returns calculated diffusion coefficient at reaction temperature. The third argument is a_v_dif, the final parameter in the definition of -viscosity in SOLUTION_SPECIES.

SI.description: Saturation index of a phase, log 10 of the ion activity product divided by equilibrium constant. For gases, this value is equal to log10(fugacity). For ideal gases, fugacity equals partial pressure. For Peng-Robinson gases, the Basic functions PR_P and PR_PHI can be used to obtain the gas partial pressure and the fugacity coefficient.

SIM_NO.description: Simulation number, equals one more than the number of END statements before current simulation.

SIM_TIME.description: Time from the beginning of a kinetic batch-reaction or transport calculation, in seconds.

SOLN_VOL.description: Volume of the solution, in liters.

SPECIES_FORMULA$.description: SPECIES_FORMULA$ returns a string that contains the type of the species--aq, ex, surf, or none if the species name is not found. In addition, values are returned for count, elt$, and coef. Count is the dimension of the elt$ and coef arrays. Elt$ is a character array with the name of each element in the chemical formula for the species plus an entry for charge (the charge number of the species).

SR.description: Saturation ratio of a phase, , ion activity product divided by equilibrium constant. For gases, SR returns the fugacity of the gas (P*phi/1 atm).

STEP.signature: FOR i = n1 TO n2 STEP n3
STEP.description: Increment of a FOR loop counter (default 1).

STEP_NO.description: Step number in batch-reaction calculations, or shift number in ADVECTION and TRANSPORT calculations.

STR$.description: Convert number to a string. The string may or may not have an exponential format depending on the value of a.

STR_E$.description: Converts number (a) to a string with exponential format (for example, -1.234e-002). The width of the string is w (or longer if more characters are needed), and the number of decimal places is d.

STR_F$.description: Converts number (a) to a string that has no exponent (for example, -0.01234). The width of the string is w (or longer if more characters are needed), and the number of decimal places is d.

SUM_GAS.description: Sums number of moles of the element in gases that match the template. The template selects a set of gases. For example, a template of {C,[13C],[14C]}{O,[18O]}2 selects all the isotopic variants of CO2(g). Multiple elements at a stoichiometric position are separated by commas within braces; an asterisk (*) in the template matches any element.

SUM_SPECIES.description: Sums number of moles of the element in aqueous, exchange, and surface species that match the template. The template selects a set of species. For example, a template of *HCO3* selects all bicarbonate species. Multiple elements at a stoichiometric position are separated by commas within braces; an asterisk (*) in the template matches any element.

SUM_S_S.description: Sums number of moles of the element in the specified solid solution.

SURF.description: Number of moles of the element sorbed on the surface. The second argument should be the surface name, not the surface-site name (that is, no underscore). A redox state may be specified; for example, As or As(5) is permitted.

SYMBOL.description: USER_GRAPH plot command: sets the symbol of the current curve.

SYMBOL_SIZE.description: USER_GRAPH plot command: sets the symbol size of the current curve.

SYS.description: With a single argument, SYS calculates the number of moles of the element in all phases (solution, equilibrium phases, surfaces, exchangers, solid solutions, and gas phase) in the reaction calculation.

S_S.description: Current moles of a solid-solution component.

THEN.description: Marks the statement executed when the IF condition is true.

TIME.description: Time interval for which moles of reaction are calculated in rate programs, automatically set in the time-step algorithm of the numerical integration method, in seconds.

TO.signature: FOR i = n1 TO n2 [STEP n3]
TO.description: Upper bound of a FOR loop counter.

TOT.description: Total molality of element or element redox state. TOT(water) is total mass of water, in kilograms.

TOTAL_TIME.description: Cumulative time (seconds) including all advective (for which -time_step is defined) and advective-dispersive transport simulations from the beginning of the run or from last -initial_time identifier.

TOTMOLE.description: Moles of an element or element valence state in solution. TOTMOLE has two special values for the argument: water, moles of water in solution; and charge, equivalents of charge imbalance in solutions (same as Basic function CHARGE_BALANCE). Note the Basic function TOT returns moles per kilogram water, whereas TOTMOLE returns moles.

TRIM.description: Trims white space from the beginning and end of string a$ .

T_SC.description: The transport- or transference-number of the ion, equal to the fraction of the specific conductance contributed by the species (unitless).

VISCOS.description: Viscosity of the solution at the current conditions (milliPascal-second). However, parameters -viscosity in the definitions of SOLUTION_SPECIES have not been defined; currently the function will be set equal to the viscosity of pure water at the given conditions (same as VISCOS_0).

VISCOS_0.description: Viscosity of pure water at the current conditions (milliPascal-second).

VM.description: Returns the specific volume (cm 3 /mol) of a SOLUTION_SPECIES, relative to VM(H+) = 0, a function of temperature, pressure, and ionic strength.
